stn_the_weekly_shortfall.title: The Weekly Shortfall
stn_the_weekly_shortfall.description: Storesman Pell counts everything into Grom'gol and everything out of it, and the gap between those two numbers has been the same gap for eleven weeks. Six crates, give or take one. He has written it up as spoilage twice and did not believe it either time.
stn_the_weekly_shortfall.accept_text: A tally is the number of things, written down, so that the number cannot be argued with later, and mine says six crates a week go off the Vine Road between my south gate and the first bend. The raptors work that stretch and raptors chew. So go and work it back the other way, and when you find something chewed, bring me the stave off it.
stn_the_weekly_shortfall.turn_in_text: These are cut. Look at the end of one. A raptor leaves you a splintered end and every one of these is flat, and I have spent eleven weeks writing spoilage in my own hand while somebody walked off with the boards. I would rather have been robbed loudly. At least then the book would be right.

stn_cut_not_chewed.title: Cut, Not Chewed
stn_cut_not_chewed.description: Overseer Mokra has Pell's flat-ended stave on her table and a camp that is six crates a week light. She has had the stave in her hand since first light and has not put it down. She asks whether you can get as far as the cutline fork and back before the light goes.
stn_cut_not_chewed.accept_text: Stonehand. The stone-armed ones off the crag, and they have been working my road. I want fewer of them on it, and I want eyes on the fork where the cutline splits, because that is where the road stops being mine and starts being theirs. Do not bring me anything back. Bring me what you saw.
stn_cut_not_chewed.turn_in_text: Stacked. You are standing there telling me they stacked it. Not broken into, not eaten, not burned for the warmth of it. Stacked and squared with the lids still on. That is worse than thieves. Thieves I can post a sentry against. Somebody out there has a use for my timber and a number in their head for when they have enough of it.

stn_what_the_wood_is_for.title: What the Wood Is For
stn_what_the_wood_is_for.description: Smith Dorgun has rebuilt the same three things for three years, because nothing in this jungle seasons and nothing dry grows here. Every board in Grom'gol came off an airship. He has heard what Mokra found at the fork and he already knows what it is.
stn_what_the_wood_is_for.accept_text: Battens. Thin, dressed, cut to one length. If they are dressing boards they are not burning them, and you do not build with another camp's timber unless you have run out of your own. Get me six off the Stonehand, and keep the apes off your back while you do it. They come down the cutline for anything that smells of the camp, and my lumber smells of the camp all the way through.
stn_what_the_wood_is_for.turn_in_text: That is a lashing notch. That is a dressed edge and that is a lashing notch, and the two of them together make a scaffold batten. They are standing on my lumber to reach something higher than they can reach. Three years I have been short of board, and the trolls on that crag have been building.

stn_one_road_four_names.title: One Road, Four Names
stn_one_road_four_names.description: Attache Zul'jana has listened to a camp full of orcs call it the Vine Road for three years. It is the fourth name the road has had and the shortest. She will trade you the third for the whole length of it, top to bottom, which nobody in Grom'gol has ever walked.
stn_one_road_four_names.accept_text: You want to know what the Stonehand are building. Start with what you are standing on. Walk it from the Marosh ford at the top to the seam at the bottom, all of it, and mind the pythons where the canopy comes down to the road. Then come back and I will give you one of the older names. One of them. I am not handing you the set.
stn_one_road_four_names.turn_in_text: Zul'marosh Dakka. The stair road. It never ran south to anywhere, it ran up, and your camp put a gate on the wrong end of it and called the rest of it vines. Somebody here will ask you where you were the day the sky changed. I am not going to. I have had that answer out of eleven of you now and not one of you knew what to do with it either.

stn_the_other_half.title: The Other Half
stn_the_other_half.description: Herbalist Mossa sells the half of the jungle that will not kill you, and she buys the raw cut from a Darkspear supplier down in Booty Bay who has started quoting her a tariff instead of a price. The same bark grows two hours from the south gate.
stn_the_other_half.accept_text: Mangrove bark, strips off the water-side root and not off the trunk. The camp calls it mistvale bark, which is wrong but shorter. Dead'wa. The water that stands. Say it whichever way suits you, I am going to write the real one in my book either way. Take the strips and keep the stiltstalkers off you while you cut, because they do not rush and they do not stop.
stn_the_other_half.turn_in_text: Trunk bark. You cut the trunk. It will do for a wash and it will not do for a draught, so I will sell it as a wash and nobody will die of it. Two hours from the gate. Two hours, and I have paid a goblin's tariff for three years to have the same bark come the long way round by sea.

stn_standing_water.title: Standing Water
stn_standing_water.description: Field-Medic Sulaa has a ward full of rotting feet and a year of her own reports blaming the lagoon for it. She is asking for this quietly, at the back of her tent, and she would rather you did not mention having been asked.
stn_standing_water.accept_text: I need to know what that water does. Walk the lagoon shore and stand in it, and get the crocolisks thin enough that standing in it is a thing you can do for a while. I am not asking you to be careless with yourself. I am asking for one person who is not one of mine, and not under me, to come back and tell me whether that water rots a foot in a week.
stn_standing_water.turn_in_text: It does not. Then it is the boots. The whole camp's boots came off the airship in one lot three years ago and it was a bad lot, and the quartermaster who signed for them is still signing for things, and I have written four reports about a lagoon. I am going to ask you to leave that out of anything you say in the hall. Then I am going to go and say it to him myself.

stn_including_me.title: Including Me
stn_including_me.description: Berth-Master Zekka will tell anyone who stands still that everything in Grom'gol came off that airship, including him. He wants a crate back out of the lagoon. It went over the side of the berth stair in the camp's first season and he describes it, twice, as stores.
stn_including_me.accept_text: Camp stores. Went off the stair into the water back when the mangroves still came up to the wall, and the crocolisks moved in after, which is the only reason it is still down there. Four bundles, whatever is left dry inside them. Watch the toads more than the lizards. A toad out there does not look like anything at all until it is on you.
stn_including_me.turn_in_text: That is not stores. That is a mask, a cord, and a drum skin that has been wet for three years, and my name is on the side of the crate in the column for cargo, because that is how I came. Listed between the salt and the rope. I packed my own tribe into a camp requisition so that nobody would read it out at the foot of the stair. Keep the cord. I do not want it looked at.

stn_less_wrong_than_it_was.title: Less Wrong Than It Was
stn_less_wrong_than_it_was.description: Mapmaker Ashi has drawn the Zul'Marosh crag three times and each sheet has more stair on it than the last. She has been assuming she miscounted, because the other explanation is a ruin that is getting bigger.
stn_less_wrong_than_it_was.accept_text: The lower court first, then the mouth above it. Stand in both and count courses. Not an impression, not about that many. Count them, and bring the number back, because I have three sheets with three different numbers on them and all three of them are mine.
stn_less_wrong_than_it_was.turn_in_text: More than the last sheet. Then it is not a ruin. I have been drawing it as a ruin for two years with the little cross hatching we use for a thing that has stopped, and there is no mark on any chart I own for a thing somebody is still working on. I am going to have to invent one and then argue about it with Orgrimmar for a year.

stn_the_stair_ends_in_a_socket.title: The Stair Ends in a Socket
stn_the_stair_ends_in_a_socket.description: Scout Hanzo has been to the top of the Steps. Nobody in Grom'gol has asked him about it, because nobody in Grom'gol believed the stair went anywhere. It goes to a flat court with a socket cut in the middle of it and nothing standing in the socket.
stn_the_stair_ends_in_a_socket.accept_text: The stairwardens hold the middle flights and they hold them properly, in reliefs, which is not a thing I have seen a jungle troll bother to do. Get through enough of them to work past the second landing, and bring me stone. Loose course stone off the stair itself, the old grey stuff, from where it has fallen and not from where it is still laid.
stn_the_stair_ends_in_a_socket.turn_in_text: Five faces. The old stone is dressed on five faces and the new work is dressed on four, and you only leave the fifth rough if you know what is going on top of it. Whoever is laying that new course has never seen the stair finished. They are copying the outside of a thing. Three years of patient good work by somebody who does not know what it was for.

stn_nobody_left_who_built_it.title: Nobody Left Who Built It
stn_nobody_left_who_built_it.description: Zul'Marosh is the oldest troll work in this jungle. Zul'jana's own tribe has no story about building it and no story about leaving it, and she says a tribe with no story about a place is a tribe that was never there.
stn_nobody_left_who_built_it.accept_text: The Rotvine call themselves keepers of that stair. They are not. They are sitting in a house calling themselves the family. Their vinespeakers carry knot-cord, which is a record, and I want five of them off them. I want you to hear me say that I am asking you to take a people's writing off their bodies, because I am not going to pretend to you that it is less than that.
stn_nobody_left_who_built_it.turn_in_text: Recent. Every cord in your hand was tied inside three years. They kept nothing before that and then something started them, all at once, the way a camp starts a ledger when it has decided it owns something. Do not ask me what. I have a guess, and the guess belongs further south than here, with trolls who never stopped keeping theirs.

stn_the_long_way_round.title: The Long Way Round
stn_the_long_way_round.description: Runner Teza came back round the fen instead of through it and says she would do it again. What she has not said to anybody is that she came back without her pouch, and the fen has had it for three weeks.
stn_the_long_way_round.accept_text: This is a favour and I am asking it as one. There is a courier pouch out on the causeway short of the fen landing, in the rot where the creepers sit. Get out to the landing, get the creepers off the ground, and look where the gangplank meets the bank. I have not reported it. I would rather go on not having reported it.
stn_the_long_way_round.turn_in_text: Lamp oil. Six jars of lamp oil and a requisition number, and the number is for the stores tent I walk past every morning. I went round a fen in the dark and then worried about it for three weeks over lamp oil, and the part I cannot get out of my head is that nobody has come asking for the lamp oil either.

stn_three_flags.title: Three Flags
stn_three_flags.description: Signalman Grut runs two flags for an airship coming in and three for one that is not stopping. Three have gone up four times this season, each time with the fen smoking, and the camp has gone four weeks short on account of it.
stn_three_flags.accept_text: Four resupplies turned away off my tower and I ran the flags for every one of them. Smoke over the fen means fire, fire in a jungle means a mooring nobody will risk, and so up go three flags. Go east and find me what is burning out there. The oozes are thick on that ground. If they are what is burning, bring me a piece of one and I will take the loss myself.
stn_three_flags.turn_in_text: Gas. It is gas. Those bladders come up out of the rot and the oozes go through them like a boot through ice, and this camp has gone hungry four times for a smell. Nobody ordered those flags. I read the smoke and I ran them, on my own judgement, four times. I am going to write that down before somebody upstairs writes a kinder version of it for me.

stn_the_hill_runs_warm.title: The Hill Runs Warm
stn_the_hill_runs_warm.description: The outflow under Rotvine Hollow is what rots the fen, and Hanzo has put his hand in it twice to be sure of the one strange thing about it. It runs warm. Caves do not run warm, and the water coming out of that hill sits lower than the water standing inside it.
stn_the_hill_runs_warm.accept_text: Go in as far as the first standing water and look at the line on the wall above it. The stranglers hold the entry galleries and they come down out of the roof, so keep your head up and your back to the stone. I want a yes or a no on one thing and you do not need to go deep for it: is there more water in that hill than is coming out of it.
stn_the_hill_runs_warm.turn_in_text: Then something is holding it back. A hill that fills and does not empty has a plug in it, and a plug is either stone, which does not move on its own, or it is alive, which does. I have been reporting that outflow as weather for two years. Weather is what you call a thing you have not walked into yet.

stn_what_was_holding_it_back.title: What Was Holding It Back
stn_what_was_holding_it_back.description: Zul'jana has heard Hanzo's answer and did not need the second half of it. The Rotvine did not name their hill after the rot, she says. They named the rot after the hill, and they were right to.
stn_what_was_holding_it_back.accept_text: Rootmaw. A root mass with a mouth grown across the throat of the lower gallery, and it has been drinking that cistern since before anybody alive started counting. Take it out of the water. And bring me the tokens off the drowned down there, and look at the marks on them before you take anything, because the drowned in that hill are not Rotvine and never were.
stn_what_was_holding_it_back.turn_in_text: Stairkeepers. That token is a count of courses, which is how a keeper signed for the stair he kept, and the number cut into these is bigger than the stair is. The stair was taller. Somebody took the top off it and left no story about doing it, and the Rotvine up there are building back toward a number they found written on a dead man.

stn_hapka_still_counting.title: Hap'ka, Still Counting
stn_hapka_still_counting.description: Overseer Mokra has four turned-away resupplies, a fen that stinks when it rains, and a cistern in the hill above it that has just started draining into her water. She is not interested in the stair. She is interested in the smell.
stn_hapka_still_counting.accept_text: Whatever is at the bottom of that hill is in my water now, and a berth-master will not bring an airship down into a stink. The Rotvine sent one of their own up there to keep the stair for them and he drowned doing it, and by every account he has not let that stop him. Go down to the sump and finish it, and bring me whatever he is carrying, because he is carrying something.
stn_hapka_still_counting.turn_in_text: Cord. Knotted cord, wet through, and three years of it by the length. Take it to the attache. She read it in front of me, she rolled it up, and she told me it was not for me. Three years I have held this camp and I have just been told politely, in my own hall, that the thing I paid for is not mine to read. Ask her again when you are further south than this. She will not say it to me twice.

stn_keep_to_it.title: Keep To It
stn_keep_to_it.description: Sentry Vrak holds the south gate and tells everyone the same thing about the road. What she does not tell them is why the panthers have learned the gate, and she has kept it out of her reports, because the answer is in the ground outside the west wall.
stn_keep_to_it.accept_text: Greenpelts on the apron. They come right up to the wall now, in daylight, and they are not hunting the wall, they are waiting at it. Thin them off the gate and off the first bend of the road. Keep to the road while you do it. There is nothing worth seeing off it on the west side and I would take it as a courtesy if you did not go looking.
stn_keep_to_it.turn_in_text: Clear. For about a week. Three years we have put our dead outside the wall, because the ground inside the palisade is rock a spade bounces off, and they have worked out which day we do it. Are you staying? I am not making conversation. I am counting what I have got and you are either in the count or you are passing through.

stn_twelve_bunks_and_a_fire.title: Twelve Bunks and a Fire
stn_twelve_bunks_and_a_fire.description: Innkeeper Rukha has twelve bunks, a hearth and the only dry wood in Grom'gol, which is not dry. She wants resin, and she is the only person in this camp who will say out loud that she does not care where anybody came from.
stn_twelve_bunks_and_a_fire.accept_text: Resin off the buttress trees. It burns wet, which is the whole miracle of the stuff, and the boars root it out of the bark and tread it into the mulch, so you will be taking it off a boar one way or another. And before you go out there: I do not care where you are from. Not from here is the whole of it, and that is true of every single body behind this fence, mine included. Nobody else in this camp is going to say that to you, so I say it early and I say it to everyone.
stn_twelve_bunks_and_a_fire.turn_in_text: That will keep the fire honest for a month. Your name is on a bunk now. In chalk, on the post, same as everyone's. The ones who have been here since the camp landed still wander past and check theirs is still up there, every few weeks, and not one of them has ever asked me why I would rub it off. I have never rubbed one off in my life.

stn_the_baron_charges_me_to_land.title: The Baron Charges Me To Land
stn_the_baron_charges_me_to_land.description: Windrider-Keeper Pazzik pays Baron Revilgaz for the privilege of setting down in Booty Bay and has paid it every week since the camp landed. He wants a second roost that is not Booty Bay. He has already picked the coast north of the camp, without having been to look at it.
stn_the_baron_charges_me_to_land.accept_text: North end of the coast trail, past the ford. I want to know if there is sky over it. A wyvern wants open water on one side and nothing overhead on the other, and the raptors work that trail hard, so you will be earning the look. Count the raptors while you are at it. I price a route by what eats the courier, not by how far it is.
stn_the_baron_charges_me_to_land.turn_in_text: Canopy to the waterline. No roost, then, and the Baron keeps his landing fee for another year. You lot gave me a word for the thing I run off that tower, you know. Timetable. I called it the schedule for years and a schedule is what you hope for. A timetable is the thing you are late against. Best word anybody ever handed me and I did not have to pay a copper for it.

stn_the_long_haul.title: The Long Haul
stn_the_long_haul.description: Windrider-Keeper Pazzik has established, at some cost to his dignity, that there is no sky over the coast north of Grom'gol. He has therefore stopped looking for a near roost. His new plan is the longest route on any flight ledger in the Horde and he is already pricing it.
stn_the_long_haul.accept_text: No roost in a morning's flight, fine. Then we go in one hop and we go far. Over the water, up the whole length of the coast, Tarren Mill in Hillsbrad. A wyvern that flies that does not eat on the way, it eats before, and that means pressed feed, the heavy blocks, boar fat and jungle grain beaten together until it goes hard. Six blocks. The rootgrubbers give you the fat. The thornbacks will try to take it back off you, because they have been robbing my feed store since the day the store existed.
stn_the_long_haul.turn_in_text: Enough for one bird, one crossing, one way. Which is the whole of the argument, you understand. The Baron's roost I can reach twice before noon, and this one I can reach once and then I am sitting in Hillsbrad with a hungry wyvern and a landing fee of nothing at all. Nothing at all. I have been saying that number to myself for a week and it has not stopped being my favourite number.

stn_a_name_at_the_other_end.title: A Name at the Other End
stn_a_name_at_the_other_end.description: A route is not a route until somebody at the far end agrees to catch it. Pazzik has written his out in a small fast hand on both sides of the card, and he has heard there is an orc on a tower in Hillsbrad who flies the same beast he does and has nobody to fly it to.
stn_a_name_at_the_other_end.accept_text: Wind-Rider Ghulrak, Tarren Mill. Take him this and do not read it. No, read it, I do not care, it is a schedule and a price and the price is the part he will argue with. Go up on the Baron's route and change at the mill, and yes, that costs you, and yes, you are paying the fee I am trying to stop paying. Hold that thought for about nine hours and you will understand my whole position.
stn_a_name_at_the_other_end.turn_in_text: A jungle goblin wants to put a wyvern over open water for the better part of a day on the strength of a feed block. Sit down. I am not saying no. I am saying I have flown that coast and there is a stretch in the middle of it with nothing under you but water and nothing over you but weather, and a bird that tires there does not get to tire somewhere else instead.

stn_two_roosts_one_ledger.title: Two Roosts, One Ledger
stn_two_roosts_one_ledger.description: Wind-Rider Ghulrak has flown the Hillsbrad lanes long enough to know exactly what the middle of Pazzik's route is: open water with nothing to come down on. He will put his hand to it if somebody holds that middle, and the only people flying that middle at night are dead.
stn_two_roosts_one_ledger.accept_text: Three things you should ask me before you fly anywhere, and I will answer all three, because a courier who does not know the route is cargo. Then take my endorsement west to the Sepulcher and put it in Bat Handler Odo's hand. His bats cross that water every night of the year. If he will bring a wyvern down on his tower in bad weather, the route stands. If he will not, your goblin can go on paying his Baron for the privilege of landing.
stn_two_roosts_one_ledger.turn_in_text: An orc's hand and a goblin's arithmetic, and the orc has the honesty to write down the part he cannot solve. There it is, bottom of the page, in his own letters: the middle. He has flown it. I have hung upside down in it. Those are not the same qualification and mine is the one that matters here.

stn_the_relay_signed.title: The Relay Signed
stn_the_relay_signed.description: Bat Handler Odo has read a goblin's route, an orc's endorsement, and a weather note about a jungle he will never see. He has signed it. He has also added a line at the bottom in his own hand, which is the part of the page that matters.
stn_the_relay_signed.accept_text: I will light the tower. Not for the goblin and not for the orc. For the bird, which has no say in any of this and is the one that will be hitting the water. Take it back down to your Pazzik, and tell him the line at the bottom is mine and it is not open to discussion: in bad weather the wyvern comes down on my tower and the mail goes the rest of the way on a bat. He will hate that. He will sign it.
stn_the_relay_signed.turn_in_text: He lit the tower and then he put his hand in my pocket. Bad weather and the mail goes on a bat. His bat, his route, his cut, and he knew exactly what he was doing when he wrote it under the signature instead of over it. Stamp it. Three years I have paid the Baron to let me land, and now I pay a dead man to keep my bird out of the sea, and that is still cheaper, and I am going to walk into Booty Bay and tell the Baron so with my own mouth.

stn_nothing_they_have_fought_climbs.title: Nothing They Have Fought Climbs
stn_nothing_they_have_fought_climbs.description: Drillmaster Ukko has a drill ground, a palisade, and a syllabus he has rewritten exactly once in his life. He rewrote it three years ago. He will tell you why if you ask him, and he would much rather you asked him here than worked it out on the cutline.
stn_nothing_they_have_fought_climbs.accept_text: Ask me what you like. Then go and fight something that climbs. The thornbacks come down the cutline hand over hand and they do not come at your front, they come at the top of your head, and a recruit who has only ever been hit from the front dies looking at the ground. I want you to have been hit from above before I put anybody behind you. That is not a figure of speech. That is the order of the lesson.
stn_nothing_they_have_fought_climbs.turn_in_text: You have been watching the canopy since you came back through that gate and you have not noticed you are doing it. That is the whole lesson and the jungle taught it to you in an afternoon. I have been shouting it across this ground for three years and it has never once gone in that fast.

stn_the_third_direction.title: The Third Direction
stn_the_third_direction.description: Ukko wants a climbing frame on his drill ground and there is not a length of rope in Grom'gol that has not already been spliced twice. There is, however, a great deal of vine in this jungle, and the vine is attached to something that objects to being shortened.
stn_the_third_direction.accept_text: Coil. Strangler vine, off the wet ground where it grows green and has not gone woody yet. Cut it long and cut it fresh. Seven coils, and put the pythons off it before you start, because a coilvine in the canopy is exactly the colour of the thing you are reaching for and you will only make that mistake once.
stn_the_third_direction.turn_in_text: Up. Down is the ground, forward is the gate, and up is the direction nobody drills, and now there is a frame on my ground to drill it on. First one over the top of it was a storesman's clerk with a bad leg, which is the only part of today I did not arrange. Nobody laughed. I would have had words.

stn_not_tame_fed.title: Not Tame, Fed
stn_not_tame_fed.description: Beast-Handler Kozza keeps the camp's raptor pens and the wyvern lines, and she has one rule she repeats to everybody and means every time: the animals are not tame, they are fed. The feed ran short the week the resupply turned away, and the pens have become interesting to the panthers.
stn_not_tame_fed.accept_text: Boar haunch. Not offal, not slop. Dis is not slop I be making - a raptor dat gets slop remembers it, and den she bites de hand dat brought it. Eight off the rootgrubbers, good ones, off the leg. And the greenpelts have found my pens, mon. Dey sit in the green by the line and dey wait on feeding hour the same as the birds do. Put dem off it before one of dem works out which end of the pen the gate is on.
stn_not_tame_fed.turn_in_text: Dey eat, dey settle, dey let me walk between dem. Dat is the whole of it. Nobody in dis camp has named one of dose birds and nobody is going to, because the day you name a ting you start expecting it to be grateful. Den one morning it is not grateful, and you are surprised, and surprised is how a handler loses an arm.

stn_what_the_pens_know.title: What the Pens Know
stn_what_the_pens_know.description: Kozza's raptors have gone off their feed on the same day of the week since the dry turn, and she has stopped thinking it is the feed. A penned bird knows what is moving on the road outside the fence better than the sentry on the gate does, and Kozza has been reading hers for three seasons.
stn_what_the_pens_know.accept_text: Sit up on de rail and ask me. Dis is not a ting I can hand you in a sack and it is not a ting I am going to carry up to the overseer's table on my own, because what I have is a shape in my head, and a shape in your head is worth nothing at all until somebody else has heard it out loud and not laughed.
stn_what_the_pens_know.turn_in_text: Dere. Now it is said, and now it is two of us dat know it, and if I go off dis rail tomorrow the camp still has it. Tell the overseer if you like. She will want it as a number and I have not got a number. I have got birds, and birds do not count. Dey just stop eating.

stn_signed_for_twice.title: Signed For Twice
stn_signed_for_twice.description: Berth-Master Zekka has a grant out of Booty Bay with the Baron's stamp on it and a date in a much smaller hand underneath the stamp. He has read it four times. He would like somebody else to walk it across the camp to the overseer, because he has worked out what it means and does not want to be the one holding it when she does.
stn_signed_for_twice.accept_text: It is a berth. A berth in the Baron's own harbour, granted to this camp, for this camp's airship, in perpetuity, at a rate. Read the rate. Then read the little date under the stamp, which is not the day he signed it, it is the day he decided we were the sort of camp that would one day have to ask. Take it to the overseer. I have signed for everything that came off that stair. I am not signing for this.
stn_signed_for_twice.turn_in_text: In perpetuity. A goblin has granted me, in perpetuity, the right to go on paying him for the one thing this camp cannot do without, and he dated the decision to the season we landed. He has been sitting on it for three years waiting for me to need the paper badly enough to come and ask for it. Put it on the table. Not in the chest. On the table, where I can look at it a while.

stn_four_reports_and_a_boot.title: Four Reports and a Boot
stn_four_reports_and_a_boot.description: Field-Medic Sulaa said it to the quartermaster's face and he wrote it down and nothing happened, because the lot of boots she wants condemned was signed for by the only man whose signature could condemn it. So she has given up on the boots and started on the feet instead.
stn_four_reports_and_a_boot.accept_text: There is a tuber in the fen rot. Pale, about a thumb long, and it will pull water out of anything you pack it against. Seven, and they sit under the standing water, which means the toads - and a toad out there is a stone until it is on your back. I cannot condemn a boot. I can keep a foot dry inside one, and I have a ward of eleven men who would take that trade before breakfast.
stn_four_reports_and_a_boot.turn_in_text: A cloth, a tuber, and a foot dry for a day and a half. That is not a cure. That is a delay, and a delay is most of medicine in a place like this. He is still signing, by the way. Boots, rope, salt, bandages. Every requisition that comes off that stair has his hand at the bottom of it and not one person in this camp has ever asked him to stop.

stn_in_the_count.title: In the Count
stn_in_the_count.description: Sentry Vrak asked you once, as a courtesy, not to look at the ground outside the west wall. You looked or you did not. Either way she has stopped asking for courtesies and started asking for the thing she should have put in a report two years ago.
stn_in_the_count.accept_text: The greenpelts have the day. They know which day we carry out, they are on the apron before we are, and thinning them buys a week and then it is the same week over again. So. The innkeeper keeps a post with every name in this camp on it in chalk, and that post is the only honest list of us there is. I want a second one on it. The ones outside the wall. I am asking you because you are not on that post and nobody who is would carry this across the camp. That is not an insult. That is the reason.
stn_in_the_count.turn_in_text: She wants them chalked on the same post as the living. Same post, under a line, same chalk. She has been carrying that for two years and she has walked past this door every day of it. Well, I have the chalk and I have the post and I am not the one who has to explain it to the overseer, so it goes up tonight. You want the part that got me? She asked whether she was allowed to be on both.

stn_a_mark_for_a_thing_still_being_made.title: A Mark for a Thing Still Being Made
stn_a_mark_for_a_thing_still_being_made.description: Mapmaker Ashi invented a chart mark for a ruin that somebody is still working on. That took her an afternoon. Defending it will take her a year, and a new mark with only one site under it is not a mark, it is a mistake with a symbol on top of it.
stn_a_mark_for_a_thing_still_being_made.accept_text: Two sites or the survey office files it as a special case and buries it under the stair. So: chips off the new relief work up on the Steps, the four-faced stuff and not the old grey, six of them. Then go and stand in the cutline camp above the fork, where somebody has been stacking our timber into something that has a shape to it. If it has a shape, it is a site, and if it is a site I have two.
stn_a_mark_for_a_thing_still_being_made.turn_in_text: Two sites. Then it is a mark. I will send it north and it will come back corrected, because there is a clerk in the survey office who has been correcting my sheets for a year and a half and has never been further south than the Barrens. He came through the same season you did. He learned this jungle off sheets I drew and now he knows it better than I do on paper, and paper is what they keep. I am going to win this one. It will take until the dry turn and I am going to win it.
